newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BOND PRICES STATIC, YIELD GAP NARROWING.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BOND PRICES STATIC, YIELD GAP NARROWING.

text.p: Danish bond prices were near static while the 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed in a quiet pre-Christmas market on Monday, with rises possible.
"The benchmark 2006 bond should trade within the 109.00-40 range today, the Danish bond market should outperform Germany but it is the German March bund which is setting the pace," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.10 point from Monday's close at 109.08 but still 0.47 point short of last Thursday's close, before Fed chairman Alan Greenspan alarmed markets with a warning against "irrational exuberance."

The benchmark's turnover was 600 million crowns only despite reported foreign investor interest while its December future rose 0.22 point to 109.08 with 193 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.08 point to 85.98.
The crown traded at 3.8274 per mark at 1140 gmt, unchanged from the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 88 during the course of the morning.
